premise: At Kisaragi Middle School, a small garden club tends a few pots of tomatoes on the rooftop. When the principal announces that the roof will be turned into solar panels unless the club can prove it grows something worthwhile, the members must save their only dying plant. Their scrambled, argumentative efforts over three weeks pull in a grumpy former member and a sleepy advisor who knows more than he admits.

characters.role: The club president, bright and blunt, who speaks in short, determined sentences and never gives up on a plant.
A former club member who quit after a failed harvest, sarcastic and dry, hiding his care behind jokes.
A second-year who measures everything and speaks in numbers, often starting sentences with 'technically'.
A cheerful first-year who names every plant and container, speaking in exclamations and cheerful nonsense.
The lazy-seeming club advisor who speaks in calm, philosophical remarks and will do almost anything for melon bread.
A strict, formal principal who speaks in rules and deadlines but is secretly fond of good tomatoes.

ja: 屋上の小さな畑に、今日も風が吹きます。
en: On the small rooftop garden, the wind blows again today.

ja: トマトは、まだ赤くなっていません。
en: The tomatoes have not turned red yet.

ja: さあ、今日のお話を始めましょう。
en: Well then, let's begin today's story.
Continued on the rooftop, next time.

scenes.summary: Haru stands alone on the roof at dawn, watering a single wilting tomato plant. She tells the plant out loud that the club will not let it die.

en: Just a little more water, okay?

ja: 昨日より、ちょっと葉が硬い。
en: Your leaves are stiffer than yesterday.

ja: 絶対に、枯らさないから。
en: I mean it. You're not dying on me.

ja: 今日から、ちゃんと世話する。
en: We only have three weeks. Starting today, I'll take proper care of you.

ja: 校長先生が言ったでしょ。
屋上がソーラーパネルになるって。
en: That this roof is becoming solar panels.

ja: 私も、リクも、トモエも、みのりも。
en: Nobody in the club has given up, not me, not Riku, not anyone.

ja: あんたも、まだ諦めないでよね。
en: And you'd better not give up either.

scenes.summary: Riku and Tomoe argue on the stairs about whether the plant is dead. Riku calls it a lost cause, while Tomoe insists it is only thirsty.

ja: 行くよ！ あの子、待ってるもん。
en: Of course! She's waiting for me.

ja: 待ってない。もう死んでる。
葉っぱ、全部しおれてるじゃん。
en: Look at her leaves. Every single one is limp.

ja: しおれてるだけ！ 喉かわいてるんだよ。
en: They're just droopy. She's parched, that's all.

ja: 三日前から水やってんだろ。
en: We've been watering her for three days.

ja: じゃあ、もっとあげればいいの！
根っこが腐ってたら、水やっても意味ないの。
en: If the roots are rotting, more water makes it worse.
Did you actually look at the roots?
I don't need to. I can tell.

ja: 同じ形で枯れたんだよ。
en: Last year was the same. Same way, same wilt.

ja: 去年も、今年も、枯れるもんは枯れるの。
en: Every year it's the same. What dies, dies.

ja: 植物は息しないけどな。
ねえ、茎、触ってみた？ 硬いよ。
en: Did you touch the stem? It's still firm.

ja: 硬いのは、乾いてるからだ。
en: It's firm because it's dried out.

ja: 乾いてるなら、まだ戻るってことでしょ！
en: Then it can come back, right?

ja: なんでそう言い切れるんだよ。
だって、ハルちゃんが諦めてないもん。
en: Because Haru hasn't given up, so neither will we.

ja: 行かねえって言っただろ。
en: I told you, I'm not coming.

ja: ふーん、じゃあ、ひとりでやる。
en: Fine. I'll do it alone, then.

scenes.summary: Principal Mitsuhashi tells the club that the roof becomes solar panels after the spring festival unless they can prove the garden grows something useful. He states the rule flatly and walks away.

ja: 全員、集まってください。
春の文化祭のあと、屋上は太陽光パネルになります。
en: After the spring festival, the roof becomes solar panels.

ja: 屋上は、私たちの畑です！
ただし、園芸部が役に立つ作物を育てていると
証明できれば、計画は白紙に戻す。
en: Unless the club proves it grows something useful, the plan is scrapped.

ja: 役に立つって、どういう基準ですか。
en: What counts as useful? What's the standard?

ja: 人が食べられて、収穫できるもの。
期限は文化祭の前日まで。
en: The deadline is the day before the spring festival.

ja: 三週間しかないんですよ！
苗から育てたら間に合いません！
en: We only have three weeks! Starting from seedlings won't make it in time.

ja: 三週間で何ができるかは、君たちが考えることだ。
en: What you can do in three weeks is for you to work out.
That's all I have to say.

ja: トマト、お好きなんですか？
水やりは、時間を守って。
en: Keep your voices down up here.

ja: 声が大きいと苦情が来る。
en: Complaints come in when it's loud.

ja: 期限を過ぎれば、パネルは設置される。
en: After the deadline, the panels go up. No exceptions.

scenes.summary: Minori tests the soil and reports to the club that it is packed too tightly and drains badly. She explains the numbers while Tomoe asks what 'drains' means.

ja: 技術的に言うと、良くない。
ペーハーって何！？ おいしいの？
食べ物じゃない。酸性かアルカリ性かの数字。
en: It's not food. It's a number for acid or alkaline.

ja: それ、みのりの一番好きな話題だろ。
en: That's your favorite topic, isn't it?

ja: 好きじゃない。必要な情報。
en: It's not a favorite. It's necessary data.

ja: 百ミリリットルの水が染み込むのに、十一分かかった。
en: The real problem is drainage. Pouring a hundred milliliters took eleven minutes to soak in.

ja: 水が土から抜けていくこと。
en: How fast water runs out of the soil.
Run out... like a snake shedding?

ja: そういう意味じゃない。
適正は一分から三分。十一分は遅すぎる。
en: Healthy soil takes one to three minutes. Eleven is far too slow.

ja: 土が固い。指で押すと十二センチ下で止まる。
en: The soil is packed hard. My finger stopped at twelve centimeters.
The roots can't grow through it.

ja: 技術的には、根が酸素を取り込めない状態。
en: Technically, the roots can't get enough oxygen.

ja: 酸素！ 息ができないの？ トマトさん、ごめんね！
en: Oxygen! It can't breathe? Sorry, Tomato-san!

ja: じゃあ、どうすればいい？
まず砂と腐葉土を混ぜて、土を崩す。
鉢の底の穴も、三つは必要。
en: First we break up the soil with sand and compost. We need at least three drainage holes too.

ja: 穴なんか、あけりゃいいだろ。
en: Just poke some holes, how hard can it be?

ja: 穴の位置と数を決めないと、水が溜まる。
en: The position and number matter, or water pools at the bottom.

ja: 計算は趣味じゃない。責任。
en: It's not a hobby. It's responsibility.

ja: 穴あけるの、ちょっとかわいそう！
en: Making holes in them seems mean!

ja: 数字は、あとで記録する。
en: Right, I'll log the numbers later.

ja: 記録！ ノート、一番かわいいやつ使う！
en: A log! I'll use my cutest notebook!

ja: 技術的に、それが一番いい案。
en: Technically, that's the best idea anyone's had today.

scenes.summary: Miyashita-sensei lounges by the fence and says the plant has a root problem, not a water problem. He jokes that he will only help for melon bread.

ja: 宮下先生、いるなら手伝って！
en: Sensei, if you're there, help us!

ja: いるよ。ずっとここにいる。
en: I'm here. I've been here the whole time.

ja: 君が水をやり始めたときから。
en: Since you started watering it at dawn.

ja: 声かけたら、手伝わされるでしょ。
en: If I said something, you'd make me help.

ja: 当たり前！ 先生の仕事だよ！

en: Did you look at the roots?

ja: 見たよ。見なくても分かる。
en: I did. You don't need to look to know.
We've been watering it every day!

ja: 水の問題じゃない。根っこの問題。
en: It's not a water problem. It's a root problem.

ja: だから、根が息できてない。
en: That's exactly it. The roots can't breathe.

ja: 土が固すぎる。水が溜まって、根が溺れてる。
en: The soil's too packed. Water pools and the roots drown.

ja: 技術的に、それで合ってる。
小泉、どこから聞いてたの。
en: Koizumi, how long were you listening?

ja: 報告に来たら、先生がもう喋ってた。
en: I came to report, and Sensei was already talking.

ja: ふうん。じゃあ、どうすればいいの。
en: Hmm. So what do we do?

ja: 土を崩して、鉢を替える。根は傷つけずに。
en: Break up the soil, then repot it.
Be careful not to hurt the roots.

ja: ……先生、それ前にも言ってたよね。
言ったよ。何回でも言う。
en: I did. I'll keep saying it.
Melon bread, and one won't be enough.

ja: はい出た、メロンパン商法。
en: There it is, the melon bread racket.

ja: 商法って言うな。対価だよ、対価。
en: Don't call it a racket. It's a fair trade.

ja: 買うのは僕らでいい。先生は見てて。
en: We'll buy it. You just watch from there.

ja: 見てるだけでも、ちょっと疲れるからさ。
en: Even watching wears me out, you know.

scenes.summary: Riku admits to Haru that he quit last year after the last tomato failed. He agrees to help if the club keeps his secret, and Haru promises.

ja: 大和田くん、どうして辞めたの？

en: Where's that coming from all of a sudden?
No reason. I just got bored.

ja: 最後のトマト、覚えてる？
en: Do you remember the last tomato?

ja: 実が赤くなる前に、全部割れた。
水やりは僕の担当だった。
en: They all split before they ripened. Watering was my job.

ja: 毎日見てたのに、気づけなかった。
en: I checked them every day and still missed it.

ja: 辞めたっていうか、逃げた。
en: "Quit" is a nice word for it. I ran.

ja: 逃げたとは、違うと思う。
en: I don't think running is the right word.

ja: 一個も食べられなかった。
en: We didn't get to eat a single one.

ja: それが一番きつかった。
大和田くん、今もトマト好きなんだね。
en: You still like tomatoes, don't you, Owada?

ja: 好きじゃない。気になるだけ。
じゃあ、手伝ってくれる？
このこと、誰にも言わないで。

en: Especially Tomoe. She'll make a huge deal out of it.

ja: 僕が割ったって、知られたくない。
en: I don't want anyone to know I'm the one who lost them.

ja: でも、リクもちゃんと来てね。
en: But you have to show up too, okay?

ja: 来なかったら、私が屋上まで引っ張ってく。
en: If you don't come, I'll drag you up to the roof myself.

scenes.summary: The members carry bags of soil up the stairs, and Tomoe tries to name each container while Riku mocks the names. Minori tells them to stop and lift properly.

ja: ちょっと、一人で二袋はダメ。
en: Hey, you're not carrying two bags alone.
I'm fine. I can handle it.

ja: 階段で転んだら、土まみれだよ。
en: If you trip on these stairs, you'll be covered in soil. Seriously, stop.

ja: 名前はもうつけた。ポットン。

en: Pottun? What kind of name is that?

ja: 鉢にかわいいって、どうなの。
en: Cute for a pot? That's a stretch.

ja: じゃあリクはなんて呼ぶの。
en: Then what would you call it, Riku?

ja: 事実を言っただけだろ。
この土の袋はモグモグ。
en: And this soil bag is Mogu-mogu.

ja: 土が食べられるわけないじゃん。
名前の意味は、まだ考えてない。
en: I haven't figured out what the name means yet.
Let's just get these up first.
Torii, stop talking on the stairs.
Everyone, stop right where you are.

ja: 腰で持つから、腰を痛めるの。
en: You're lifting with your back, which is how people get hurt. Bend your knees.
Pull the bag in close to your body.

ja: 理屈では、腰の負担が半分になる。
en: In theory, that cuts the strain on your lower back roughly in half.

ja: 測ったわけじゃないけど。
en: I didn't measure it, but it's roughly that.

ja: 測ってないのに、数字言うな。
en: You haven't measured anything and you're still throwing out numbers.

ja: 楽なの、ちょっと悔しい。
en: It's easier, and I'm a little annoyed about it.

ja: 残り十袋、一人二袋ずつ。

en: Line the pots up in a row over there.

ja: やった、ポットンが一番上！
en: Yes! Pottun gets the top spot!
They're all the same pot, Tomoe.

scenes.summary: Minori and Haru debate the plan, with Minori saying one harvest in two months is impossible from this plant. Haru argues they need seedlings, and Minori cites the number of growing days.

ja: 二か月で一回の収穫、この株じゃ無理。
en: One harvest in two months from this plant? Impossible.

ja: 根が詰まってて、水もはけてない。
en: The roots are packed in, and the water isn't draining at all.

ja: 根が詰まってても、まだ生きてる。
en: Even with cramped roots, it's still alive.

ja: 生きてるのと、実をつけるのは別の話。
en: Staying alive and bearing fruit are different things.
We don't have enough days for that.

ja: 苗でも、植え替えで一週間は止まる。
en: Even seedlings stall for about a week after transplanting.

ja: 植えたら花が咲いて、受粉して、実が膨らむ。
en: Then it flowers, gets pollinated, and the fruit swells.

ja: 一段ずつ、時間がかかるの。
en: Each step takes its own time.

ja: 早い品種でも、植えてから五十五日くらい。
en: Even an early variety needs about fifty-five days after planting.
Two months is sixty days, so the margin is only five days.

ja: 五日あれば十分でしょ。
天気が崩れて、雨が続いたら、それでおしまい。
en: One stretch of rain and it's over. Pollen won't set when it's wet like that.

ja: 雨が続くと、花粉がくっつかないの。
en: Keep raining and the pollen won't stick.

ja: そこまで計算してるの？
じゃあ、ゼロって言わないで。

en: I never said zero. I said the margin is tight.
...If it's not zero, then we do it.

ja: 小泉、それ数字で出して。
植え付けの日から五十五日。
en: Planting day plus fifty-five days is harvest.
So the planting date is the number that matters.

ja: 植えるのは、遅くとも十八日。
en: We plant by the eighteenth at the latest.
Next week's Saturday. Technically, that's the eighteenth.

ja: 待って。苗はどこで買うの？
en: Wait. Where are we buying the seedlings?

ja: 商店街の園芸店。でも高いの。
en: The garden shop on the shopping street. But they're expensive.

scenes.summary: Tomoe finds an old seed packet in the shed and reads the faded label aloud, asking what it means. Riku says it is from a variety nobody sells anymore.

en: It was at the back of the shed, in a paper bag.

ja: 字がかすれてて、読みにくい。
en: The writing's so faded it's hard to read.
What does that mean? Is it a name?
Don't go digging through other people's stuff.

ja: 埃まみれの袋、よく見つけたな。
en: Find a dusty bag like that, and you still managed to find it.

ja: 発芽率、書いてないかな。
en: I wonder if it lists a germination rate.

ja: そんな品種、もう誰も売ってない。
en: Not for years, not even the big nurseries.

ja: 昔、商店街の店で扱ってたやつだよ。
en: The shop on the shopping street used to carry it.

ja: じゃあ、めずらしいんだ！
めずらしいことと、育つことは別。
en: Rare and growable are different things. Technically.

ja: 乾燥して保存されてたなら、可能性はある。
en: If they were kept dry, there's a chance.
But old seeds lose vigor every year.
That's over ten years old, you know.

ja: 長生きの問題じゃない。
en: It's not about how long they last.
Serious. If there's no other option, we try it.

ja: 一粒ずつ数えて、蒔きましょう。
en: Let's count them out and sow them one at a time.
And we're giving them names too!

ja: もう決めた！一号はルビーちゃん！
en: Already decided! Number one is Ruby-chan!

ja: 手伝ってくれるでしょ？

scenes.summary: Mitsuhashi passes the roof and hears Haru shouting at the pots. He tells her to keep her voice down and reminds her of the deadline.

ja: 何をしているんですか、真白さん。
en: What exactly are you doing up here, Mashiro?

ja: 声が屋上から三階まで届いています。
en: Your voice is carrying all the way down to the third floor.

ja: 植物に話しかけてただけです！
en: I was only talking to the plants!
Yes. So they can hear me.

ja: 植物は、叫んでも育ちません。
en: Plants don't grow faster because you shout at them.

ja: あきらめないって伝えたくて。
大きいほうが届く気がするんです。
en: I want them to know we won't give up. Loud just feels like it reaches them.

ja: 届きません。ただの騒音です。
en: It doesn't reach them. It's just noise.

ja: 騒音と言われたくなければ、静かにしなさい。
en: If you don't want it called noise, then be quiet.

ja: 文化祭のあと、この屋上はソーラーパネルになります。
en: After the spring festival, this roof becomes solar panels.

ja: だから今、育ててるんです。
en: I know. That's why we're growing it now.

ja: 植物を証明に使うなら、まず実を見せなさい。
en: If you're using plants as proof, show me fruit first.

ja: 実がなったら、見せます！
en: When it fruits, I'll show you!

ja: 今は葉しかありません。
en: Right now there's nothing but leaves.
Leaves mean it's still alive, at least.

ja: 校長先生も、トマト好きなんですか？
en: Do you like tomatoes too, Principal?

ja: 質問の意図が分かりません。
en: I don't see what that has to do with anything.

ja: さっき、赤いのを見てましたよね。
en: Earlier you were looking at the red one, weren't you?

ja: 通りかかっただけです。
en: I wasn't looking. I was just passing by.

ja: 真白さん、声を落としなさい。
えっ、怒ってないんですか？
規則は、全員が同じ条件で動くためにあります。
en: Rules exist so everyone plays by the same terms.

ja: 期限内に、証明してください。

en: I will prove it! I promise!

scenes.summary: At dusk, Riku and Haru repot the plant together, and Riku says it can still grow back. Haru thanks him, and he pretends not to hear.

ja: うわ、根っこが鉢の形になってる。
en: Ugh, the roots have taken the shape of the pot.

ja: 無理にほどくと、折れるぞ。
en: Pull too hard and they'll snap.

ja: 手つき、意外と丁寧だな。
褒めてない。 観察だ。
en: Not a compliment. Just an observation.
Which new soil are we using?

ja: 小泉が測ったやつ。 水はけがいいほう。
en: The one Koizumi tested, the one that drains better.

ja: 水はけ……。 トモエに説明しといて。
en: Drains... Better explain that to Tomoe later.

ja: 根が、まだ白い。 生きてる。
en: The roots are still white. It's alive.

ja: 空、オレンジになってきた。
en: The sky's turning orange. Sunset's pretty.

ja: 夕方の水やりは、少なめだよね。
en: Evening watering should be light, right?

ja: 少しでいい。 根が腐るから。
en: Just a little. Too much and the roots rot.
Look at you, knowing all that.

ja: 土の下で、まだ頑張ってる。
en: It's still fighting down there in the soil.

ja: 戻るかどうかは、分からない。
en: No idea if it'll come back.
Didn't hear a thing. It's just the wind.
The wind sounds gentle today, doesn't it?

scenes.summary: Tomoe bounces on the roof and announces that next week they will try planting seedlings. She teases that someone is going to get soaked in the process.

ja: 植えたいときが、植え時！
en: Whenever you want to plant is planting time!

ja: 厳密には、本葉が出てからが理想。
en: Technically, it's best once the true leaves come out.
Too early, and they won't survive the move.
The forecast says rain, so someone's getting soaked!
It's totally going to be you!
You're the one who always holds the hose.

ja: 濡れてもいい。苗が育つなら。
en: I don't mind getting wet, as long as they grow.

scenes.summary: Tomoe proudly shows off twelve seedlings in paper cups and says they are all alive. Riku points out that one is already lying flat, and Tomoe refuses to hear it.

ja: じゃーん！ 十二個、ぜんぶ発芽しました！
えっ、すごい！ 本当に全部？
en: Wow! All of them? For real?

ja: はい！ 一個も欠けてません！

en: And every single one is healthy!

ja: 元気かどうかは、まだ分からないだろ。
en: You can't tell if they're healthy yet.

ja: 分かります！ 見たら分かります！
en: I can! You can tell just by looking!

ja: じゃあ、その左から三番目。
en: Then that one, third from the left.

ja: え、この子？ 元気ですよ、ほら。
完全に横になってるだろ。
en: She's lying flat, Tomoe. Completely flat.

ja: 寝てるだけです！ 植物も休みますから！
en: Plants need breaks too, you know!

ja: 植物は寝ないんだよ、普通は。
うーん、この子はちょっと個性派なんです！
en: Hmm, she's just a bit of an individualist!

ja: トモエ、名前までつけてるの？
もちろん！ 左から、トマ子、トマ太、
en: Of course! From the left, Tomako, Tomata, Tomami!

ja: 名前の方が大事なんです！ あ、この子はナナちゃん！
en: Names matter more! Oh, this one's Nana-chan!

ja: 倒れてるのがナナちゃん？
en: The one lying down is Nana-chan?

ja: はい！ 今は横になって考え中です。
大丈夫、きっと起きます！
en: Yes! She's lying down, thinking things over. She'll get up, I'm sure!

ja: 聞こえません！ 聞こえません！
en: I can't hear you! I can't hear you!

ja: リク、その言い方はちょっと……
優しく言ったら、もう一回倒れるよ。
en: Say it gently and she'll fall over again.

scenes.summary: Minori checks the leaves under a magnifier and finds tiny green insects. She warns Haru that they could spread to every plant on the roof.

en: Haru, come here for a second.

ja: この葉っぱ、拡大鏡で見て。
en: Look at this leaf through the magnifier.

ja: 裏側に、小さい緑の虫がいる。
en: There are tiny green bugs on the underside.
That's just on this one leaf.

ja: この一枚だけで十七匹？
en: Seventeen on this one leaf alone?

ja: 技術的には、見えてるだけでもっといる。
en: Technically, there are more. I only counted the ones I can see.

ja: 増えるのが速いの。一匹で何十匹にもなる。
en: They multiply fast. One can turn into dozens in a week.

ja: 待って、それって全部の鉢に？
en: Wait, could it spread to all the pots?

ja: 葉っぱ同士が触れても移る。
en: Yes, the wind carries them, and they move leaf to leaf too.
That means every plant on the roof.

ja: トマトも、ナナちゃんも、ぜんぶ。
en: The tomatoes, Nana-chan, all of them.

ja: ナナちゃんは今、横になってる。
今すぐ、全部の鉢を見る。
en: Let's check every pot right now, starting at the edge.

ja: 一つずつ、葉の裏を見る。
en: One by one, check under every leaf.
So how do we get rid of them?

ja: 石けん水で洗い流せると思う。
en: I think a soap spray should wash them off.

ja: でも、薬を使うなら校長に……。
en: But if we use anything stronger, we'll need the principal's okay—

ja: 三橋校長に言わなきゃだめ？
en: Do we have to tell Mitsuhashi?
He's going to find out anyway.

ja: ハル、隠すのは良くない。
en: Hiding it isn't right, Haru. Let's be honest.

ja: 今はまだ、数値が足りない。
en: We don't have enough data yet.

ja: 数字で言えるものだけ。
en: I'll only bring numbers to the principal, then we decide.

ja: 好きにして。でも、私も見る。
en: Do what you want. But I'm watching you do it.

scenes.summary: Mitsuhashi climbs up to check progress and asks for a written schedule. Haru hands him a list, and he notices it has no harvest date before the festival.

ja: 校長先生、屋上まで来たんですか？
en: Principal, you actually came all the way up here?

ja: 進捗の確認も校長の仕事だ。
en: Checking progress is part of my job. Don't look so surprised.

ja: はあ……七十二段。誰か手すりを。
en: Haa... seventy-two steps. Someone please install a railing.

ja: 手すりは予算申請中です。
en: The railing is still waiting on budget approval.

ja: そういう返事は聞いていない。
en: Hand me the schedule. In writing.

ja: あります！ちょっと待って！

en: 1. Water every morning at seven. 2. Check leaves. 3. Grafting practice.
I'll read it from the top.

ja: 水やり、観察、接ぎ木、防虫。
防虫は昨日始めたばかりだろう。
en: Pest control only started yesterday, hasn't it?

ja: 収穫日が書かれていない。
en: There's no harvest date on here.

ja: それは……まだ決めてないんです。
en: That... we haven't settled that yet.

ja: 決めていない、では困る。
en: "Not decided" isn't an answer I can accept.

ja: 技術的には、開花まで最低四十日です。
実がなるまでは、もっとかかります。
en: Technically, it's at least forty days from flowering to ripe fruit.

ja: 四十日。祭りまでは何日だ？
en: Forty days. How many days until the festival?
The math doesn't work, does it?

ja: 植物は締切を読めないんで。
事実を言っただけです。
一番左、支柱のやつです！
en: The far left one, by the stake!

ja: 名前はロビン！元気だよ！
en: Her name's Robin! She's doing great!

ja: 元気なのは名前だけだ。
en: Only the name is doing great.

ja: 水は足りているはずだが。
en: Its leaves are curling. It should be getting enough water, though.

ja: 水の量をもう一度見直せ。
en: Recheck how much water it gets.

ja: 校長、そのトマト、お気に入りですか？
en: Principal, is that tomato your favorite?
It just has a nice shape.

scenes.summary: Miyashita-sensei shows the club how to graft by splicing two stems together with tape. He says the root can be stronger than the fruit, and jokes that he learned it from a melon-bread vendor.

ja: 今日はトマトの接ぎ木をやるぞ。
二本の茎を、くっつけるんだ。
えっ、くっつけたら一本になるの？
en: Wait, so they become one plant?

ja: 先生、それ、ただの絆創膏じゃないですか。
en: Sensei, isn't that just a bandage?
Cut the ends at an angle, because the angle matters.

ja: 小泉さん、角度何度ですか。
技術的には、三十度前後です。
合わせたら、テープでぐるぐる巻く。
en: Then you line them up and wrap them tight with tape.

ja: きつく巻きすぎると、茎が締まるぞ。
en: Wrap too tight and you'll choke the stem.

ja: 優しく、でも離れないように。
en: Gently, but so they don't come apart.

ja: 先生、哲学っぽいこと言うのやめてください。
俺は一度も言ってない。
根っこのほうが強い場合もある。
実より大事なこともある。
en: Sometimes the root is stronger than the fruit.

ja: どうせ実は、根が育てたものだ。
en: The fruit's just what the root made.

ja: ねえ、そのテープ、どこで覚えたの？
en: Hey, where did you learn that tape trick?

ja: 駅前の、メロンパンの屋台のおじさんだ。
en: From the melon bread stall guy by the station.

ja: 接ぎ木は、あの人に教わった。
暇な日は、ずっと枝をいじってた。
en: On slow days, he'd fiddle with branches all afternoon.

ja: 先生、それ絶対嘘でしょ。
嘘じゃない。メロンパンは本物だ。
en: The melon bread is the real deal.

scenes.summary: Riku tells Haru that the tomato he grew with his grandfather died in a storm, which is why he quit. Haru tells him that failing once does not make him a failure.

ja: そのポット、ずっと見てたね。
en: You've been staring at that pot for a while.

ja: うそ。さっきからずっと。
en: Liar. You've been at it since earlier.

ja: ……昔、じいちゃんと育てたトマトがあった。
en: ...I grew a tomato with my grandpa once.
First year of middle school, that spring.

ja: 朝と夕方、毎日水やりして、支柱も二人で立てた。
en: We watered it every morning and evening, and we set the stakes up together.

ja: 実がついて、赤くなり始めた頃。
en: Then the fruit came in and started turning red, and then a typhoon hit.

ja: じいちゃんは入院してて、俺一人だった。
en: Grandpa was in hospital, so I was alone with it.

ja: 次の朝、支柱ごと折れてた。
en: By morning, the plant was snapped flat, stakes and all.

ja: 実は全部、地面に落ちてた。
en: Every tomato was lying in the dirt.

ja: 拾えるやつだけ拾って、残りは全部捨てた。
en: I picked up what I could and threw out the rest.

ja: それ以来、部活には行ってない。
en: I haven't come back to the club since.

ja: 同情とかいらないから。

en: I just keep thinking about how that must have felt.

ja: 失敗したら、もう一生ダメって？
en: So you think one failure means you're finished for good?

ja: 違う、そういう意味じゃない。
en: No, that's not what I meant.

ja: 俺のせいだった、って意味。
先輩のせいじゃないでしょ。
en: It wasn't your fault. A storm doesn't ask permission.

ja: でも、支柱を結んだの、俺だし。
en: But I tied the stakes. Badly.

ja: 結び目、ゆるかったのかも。
一回失敗しただけで、失敗者になんかならない。
en: One failure doesn't make you a failure.

ja: 私だって、もう三回枯らしてる。
en: I've killed three plants myself. Please don't tell anyone.
Really. And one of them is almost dead right now.

ja: 間に合わせる。手伝って。

scenes.summary: Haru and Riku argue over whether to tell the principal about the aphids. Haru wants honesty, while Riku wants to fix the problem quietly first, and they agree to try his way.

ja: 校長に言おう。アブラムシのこと。
en: We should tell the principal about the aphids.

ja: なんで。黙ってても、いいことないよ。
en: Why? Keeping quiet won't do any good.

ja: 言ったら、屋上取られるだろ。
en: If we tell him, they'll take the roof.
Even so, lying is not okay.

ja: 嘘じゃない。まだ言ってないだけ。
en: It's not a lie. We just haven't said it yet.

ja: 三日あれば、一匹残らず落とせる。
en: Give me three days and I'll get every last one.

ja: 三日で治るなら、先に言えば？
en: If it's fixed in three days, why not say so first?

ja: もう消えてたら説明しやすい。
en: When we report, it'll be easier if they're already gone.

ja: 隠してる間に広がったらどうすんの。
en: What if they spread while we're hiding them?

ja: 広がらせない。葉っぱ、もう全部調べた。
en: They won't. I've already checked every leaf.
Only the bottom ones are affected.

ja: うん。ミノリにも確認してもらった。
二百！？ 全然、少なくないじゃん。
en: Two hundred?! That's not a small number at all.
Get rid of them and it becomes a small number.
I don't want to hide things.

ja: 怒られるのは別にいい。
en: Getting yelled at, I can live with.

ja: 屋上がなくなったら、何もできない。
en: But if we lose the roof, we can't do anything.

ja: だから、先に直す。それから報告。
en: That's why we fix it first, then report.

ja: 結果が出れば、校長も文句言えない。
en: Backwards is fine. If the results are there, he can't complain.

ja: 正直すぎるのも、考えものだよ。
en: Being too honest can be a problem too.
I think about it every day.

ja: 分かった。リクのやり方で。三日だけね。

scenes.summary: The club sprays the leaves with a homemade soap solution, and Tomoe gets splashed in the face by accident. She laughs, and Riku tells her to stop wiping her eyes with dirty gloves.

ja: 霧吹き、葉の表も裏も全部かけて。
en: Spray every leaf, top and bottom.

ja: 石けんは百倍に薄めた。計量済み。
en: The soap's diluted a hundred times. I measured it.

ja: わーい！ シュッシュッ！
出しすぎ。葉がびしょびしょになる。
en: Too much. You'll drown the leaves.

ja: この子たちもシャワー浴びるの！
en: These guys get a shower too!

ja: 裏側も忘れずに。アブラムシはそこにいる。
en: Don't forget the undersides. That's where the aphids hide.

ja: この子はトマ吉！ 水しぶきくらえ！
en: This one's Tomakichi! Take that, splash!

ja: えっ、もう呼んじゃったもん。
統計的には、名前付きの鉢のほうが枯れにくい。
測ったことはないけど。
en: Statistically, named pots survive longer. I haven't actually measured that.

ja: じゃあ、トマ吉は強い子！

en: Ha ha, it stings! This is kind of funny, though.

ja: 大丈夫？ 本当にごめん。
en: Are you okay? I'm really sorry.

ja: 大丈夫！ 石けんの味がする！

en: A little won't hurt. Rinse it off to be safe.

ja: 手袋で目こするな。泥ついてるだろ。
en: Don't rub your eyes with those gloves. They're covered in dirt.
Dirt, and whatever the bugs left behind.

ja: 手も顔も、たまには洗うといい。
en: Hands and face. Maybe the heart too.

ja: 先生、ちょっと手伝って。
en: Sensei, could you help a little?
I'll try. Preferably after the melon bread.

ja: 三日でやるんだろ。数えとけよ。

scenes.summary: Minori and Riku argue about timing, with Minori saying the festival is too early and Riku saying a fast fix is possible. Minori agrees to wait if he clears the aphids in three days.

ja: 祭りまで十日しかないのよ。早すぎる。
en: The festival's only ten days away.

ja: 早くないって。虫くらい三日で片づく。
en: It's not too early. Bugs like that can be cleared in three days.

ja: 技術的に言えば、それは希望的観測。
en: Technically, that's wishful thinking, not a plan.

ja: 希望じゃなくて計画だよ。
en: It's not wishful. It's a plan.

ja: 計画なら、数字で見せて。
石けん液を薄めて、三回散布する。
en: Diluted soap, sprayed three times, every other day.
How many bugs are we talking about?

ja: 数えたら、直すより時間がかかるだろ。
en: Counting takes longer than fixing. I checked every leaf.

ja: 対策の前に、現状把握が先でしょ。
en: Shouldn't you assess the damage before you treat it?
I checked the undersides of every leaf.
You're a real pain, you know that?

ja: 誰かが数えないと、大和田くんは雑になるでしょ。
en: Someone has to count, or you'll get sloppy, Owada.

ja: 小泉に言われると、刺さるな。
刺さるのは、当たってるってこと。
en: A sting means I hit the mark.

ja: 校長が見に来るのは祭りの日だ。
en: The principal inspects on festival day. We can't wait.
That's exactly why it's too early.
Three days. I'll clear the bugs.

ja: ……三日で本当に消えたら、待つわ。
en: Only if they're really gone in three days will I wait.

ja: 三日後、確認しに来るから。
en: I'll come check in three days.

scenes.summary: Tomoe asks Miyashita-sensei why plants die, and he answers that plants are stubborn and so are people. Tomoe finds this oddly comforting.

ja: ねえ先生！ トマトって、なんで枯れちゃうの？
en: Hey, Sensei! Why do tomatoes die?

ja: だって、ミニたろうが寝てるんだもん！
en: Because Mini-Taro is lying down and won't get up!

ja: 寝てるわけじゃないよ。
えっ？ じゃあ、起きないの？
en: Eh? So he's not going to wake up?

ja: 起きるかどうかは、トモエ次第かな。
en: Whether he wakes up depends on you, maybe.

ja: わたし次第！？ じゃあ、水やる！
水のやりすぎも、よくないよ。
en: Too much water isn't good for him either.

ja: じゃあ！ どうすればいいの！
en: Then what am I supposed to do!

ja: 先生、ずるい！ 答えになってない！
en: That's cheating, Sensei! That's not an answer!

ja: 答えは、植物の方が知ってるからね。
en: Plants know the answer better than I do.

ja: でもさ、なんで死んじゃうのかは知りたい！
en: But I still want to know why they die!

ja: 一度決めたら、なかなか曲げない。
en: Once they've made up their minds, they don't bend easily.

ja: 人もね、同じくらい頑固だ。
ぼくは、眠いのが頑固なだけ。
en: I'm only stubborn about being sleepy.

ja: えへへ、それ先生っぽい！
じゃあ、ミニたろうも、まだ戦ってる？
根っこは、まだ働いてる。
en: Yes. The roots are still working.

ja: なんか、ちょっとほっとした。
en: Somehow that makes me feel better.
Strange. We're talking about dying, and I still feel better.

ja: 頑固なのは、いいことだよ。
生きたがってる証拠さ。
en: Being stubborn is good. It means they want to live.

scenes.summary: Mitsuhashi overhears Haru and Riku whispering on the stairs and asks what they are hiding. They lie badly, and he lets it go with a warning.

ja: 君が先に言ったんだろ。
階段で挨拶する人はいない。

en: Do we tell the principal or not?

ja: 嘘じゃない。まだ言ってないだけ。
en: We just haven't said it yet.

ja: 階段で何を話している。
en: What are you two discussing on the stairs?
If you're hiding nothing, what can't you tell me?
Your report is due by Monday.

ja: 屋上の植物は、学校の規則の下にある。
en: The plants on that roof fall under school rules.

scenes.summary: That night the club sets up a small light on the roof to watch for pests. Riku checks the grafted plant and admits to Minori that he is not sure he wants to return to the old way.

ja: わあ、葉っぱが光ってる！
光ってないです。反射です。
en: They're not glowing. Technically, it's reflection.
When light bounces back off something.
We take turns on watch. Nobody pushes themselves.
In ten minutes, how many bugs can you find?
Don't make a racket on the roof in the middle of the night.

ja: 照明が気になっただけだ。
en: I just wanted to check the light.

ja: テープ、少しゆるんでます。
触っても、大丈夫ですか？
en: Is it okay to touch it?
Wait, look here. The cut's still alive.

ja: 宮下先生の言ったこと、覚えてるんですね。
en: So you remember what Miyashita-sensei said.
I can't seem to forget it.
Do you want to go back, then?

ja: 昔のやり方に戻るのか、正直、わからない。
en: Go back to the old way? Honestly, I don't know.
It's not as simple as it used to be.

ja: 両方やればいいじゃん！

scenes.summary: Haru stands on the roof with a clipboard and teases that the principal is coming for the festival inspection. She says someone is going to get caught with mud on their face.

ja: 校長先生、祭りの前に検査に来るって。
en: The principal's coming to inspect before the festival, apparently.

ja: 三日で虫を全部取るって言ったよね。
en: You promised the bugs would be gone in three days, remember?

ja: 言ったのはリクでしょ。
en: That was your promise, not mine.

ja: 検査の日、顔に泥をつけた誰かさんが
校長に捕まるんだよね。
en: On inspection day, someone with mud on their face gets caught by the principal.
I need you up here for this.

scenes.summary: On festival morning, Miyashita-sensei arrives with a bag of melon bread and finds Tomoe jumping up and down. She shouts that the tomato is finally ripe.

ja: 朝の散歩でね、遠回りしたんだ。
en: I took the long way on my morning walk.

ja: それより、紙袋の中身は？
en: Never mind that. What's in the paper bag?

ja: 色が全部ちゃんと赤い。
en: The top one, look. It's fully red all over.

ja: 昨日まで青かったのに、今朝見たら真っ赤なの。
en: It was still green yesterday, but this morning it was bright red.

ja: さっきからずっと跳ねてる？
en: Have you been bouncing like that the whole time?

ja: 跳ねないと落ち着かないの！
en: I can't keep still when something this big happens!

ja: 実がつくまで、長かったね。
en: It took a long while for the fruit to come.
Waiting is always the hardest part, isn't it.

ja: 待って、みんな呼んでくる！
en: Wait, I'll go get everyone! Stay right here and watch!

scenes.summary: Minori counts the red tomatoes and finds exactly one, small and deep red. She insists everyone keep their hands off it while she calls it a miracle.

ja: 全部数えるから、誰も触らないで。
en: I'm counting every one, so nobody touch anything.
Red... just one, and I've checked it three times.
One? You've got to be joking.

ja: 冗談じゃないよ！ほら、あれ！
en: It's not a joke! Look, over there!

ja: 小さいけど、色が深いの。
en: It's small, but look at that deep red.
No touching it, not even a finger.

ja: 奇跡なんだから、手を離して。
en: This is a miracle. Take your hands off it.
A miracle? That's a bit much.

ja: 大げさじゃない。三週間かけて一個なの。
en: It's not an exaggeration. Three weeks to get one fruit.

ja: 待つのも、実りのうちだよ。
en: Waiting is part of the harvest too.

ja: それより、メロンパンは？
en: Anyway, did you bring the melon bread?

ja: 光の角度を合わせるから。
en: Hold on, I need to fix the angle of the light first.

ja: 直径三センチ、重さは十八グラム。
en: Technically, that's small for a tomato.
I've already got a name for it!

ja: 奇跡は、ちゃんと記録しないと。
en: A miracle has to be recorded properly before anyone touches it.

scenes.summary: Riku and Haru argue over who should present the tomato to the principal. Riku says it should be him because it was his fault, but Haru refuses.

en: I'll be the one who takes it to him.
I'm the president. That makes it my call.

ja: 枯らしたの、俺のせいだろ。
en: I'm the one who let it die. This is on me.

ja: 水やり、俺が一週間サボった。
en: I skipped watering for a week. Nobody else did that.

ja: だったら、俺が謝るのが筋だろ。
en: Then I should be the one apologizing to him. That's only fair.

ja: 謝るのは、トマトが助かってから。
en: You can apologize once the tomato's safe.
Don't decide that on your own.
I can talk just fine, you know.

ja: 二十分黙って、ずっと睨んでたくせに。
en: You stood there glaring at the principal for twenty minutes last time.

ja: あれは、考えてたんだよ。
考えてる顔じゃなかった。
en: You looked like you wanted to hit someone.

ja: 何がなるほどなんだよ。
en: What do you mean, you see?
I decided that on the spot.
Both of us, then. That works.

scenes.summary: Mitsuhashi arrives with the inspection board and asks for the report. He listens in silence while Haru explains the aphids and the grafts.

ja: 報告書を、提出してください。
ちょっと待って、まだ途中。
途中の報告書は受け付けません。
じゃあ、口頭で説明する。
en: Then I'll explain it out loud.

ja: えっと、まず一番の問題は、アブラムシ。
en: Okay. First, the biggest problem was aphids.

ja: 三週間前、葉の裏に集まってた。
en: Three weeks ago they covered the leaf undersides. Over a hundred of them.

ja: 厳密には、百四十二匹です。
en: Technically, it was a hundred and forty-two.

ja: 数字はどうでもいいだろ。
en: Who cares about the exact number?

ja: 手で取って、石鹸水で洗った。
en: We picked them off by hand
and washed the plants in soapy water.

ja: 接ぎ木は、台木を二本使った。
片方が病気になった時のため。
en: For the grafts we used two rootstocks, in case one got sick.

ja: 接ぎ口は斜めに切って、ぴったり合わせた。
en: We cut the joints at a slant
But the other one bore fruit.
That's the full report. Any questions?

ja: 報告は、長いと疲れますよ。
en: Long reports wear a person out. Don't they, Principal?

ja: 宮下先生、黙っていなさい。
次は、トマトを見せなさい。
触らないでくださいね。

scenes.summary: Mitsuhashi tastes the tomato, pauses, and says it is the best he has had since he was a child. He asks the club why they need the roof, and no one answers right away.

en: You can tell from the skin?!

ja: 技術的には、糖度は八・二です。
味は数字にしにくいです。
en: Technically, it's 8.2 Brix, but taste doesn't measure well.

ja: 子どものころに食べた味だ。
en: It tastes like the ones I ate as a child.
Those are hard to find now.

ja: 校長先生、いま笑いました？
君たちは、なぜ屋上が必要なんだ。
en: Why do you need the roof?

ja: 屋上にはトマトがあります！
en: There are tomatoes on the roof!

ja: 答えたら、通るんですか。
規則のほうが強いでしょう。
en: Even if we answer, the rules still win, right?

ja: 校長も、答えは知っているでしょう。
en: I think you already know the answer, Principal.

ja: 私たちは、ここで育てたいんです。
en: We want to grow things here. That's all.

ja: 育てるだけなら、鉢でいい。
en: If it's only growing, pots will do.

ja: 鉢じゃ、足りないんです。
屋上じゃなきゃ、だめなんです。
en: Pots aren't enough. It has to be the roof.

ja: 日当たりも、風も、違います。
en: The sunlight and the wind are different up here.

scenes.summary: Riku finally tells the group about his grandfather and says the roof is the only place he feels he belongs. He speaks honestly for once, and Haru does not interrupt.

ja: 別に、大した話じゃない。
en: It's not a big story or anything.

ja: じいちゃん、昔ここで野菜作ってた。
en: My grandfather grew vegetables up here.

ja: 昔、学校の裏で農家やってたんだ。
校舎ができて、畑は全部なくなった。
en: He farmed behind the school. When they built it up, every field was gone.

ja: じいちゃん、それがずっと悔しかったらしい。
en: I think he never got over that.

ja: 最後にここへ来たのは、中一の春。
en: The last time he came up here was the spring I started first year.

ja: 足腰弱ってたけど、トマト植えるって聞かなくて。
en: His legs were already weak, but he wouldn't listen. He insisted on planting tomatoes.

ja: 支柱の立て方、全部あいつに教わった。
en: I helped. He taught me how to set every stake.

ja: 夏に、じいちゃんは病院に入った。
en: That summer, he was admitted to the hospital.

ja: 秋には、もう戻らなかった。
en: By autumn, he wasn't coming back.

ja: 残ったトマトは、俺が収穫するしかなかった。
en: I was the one who had to harvest what was left. But it was all ruined.

ja: そう。 俺のせいで、枯らした。
en: Yes. I killed them. It was my fault.

ja: どうして、今まで言わなかったの？
en: Why didn't you tell us before?

ja: 言う理由、なかったから。
冗談で誤魔化してたほうが、楽だった。

en: But when I come up here, I can actually breathe.

ja: 教室にも、家にも、居場所なんてないけど。
en: I don't belong in the classroom or at home.

ja: ここだけは、ちゃんと俺の場所だって思える。
en: This is the only place I feel like I belong.
It's the only place that's mine.

ja: 恥ずかしいこと言ってるの、わかってる。
en: I know how embarrassing that sounds.

ja: 技術的には、今の話が一番正確。
en: Technically, that's the most accurate thing you've said all week.

ja: 植物も、ひとつの場所で育つんだよ。
en: Plants grow in one place too, you know.

ja: 大和田くん、ここにいていい。
この屋上、ちゃんと残す。
en: You're allowed to stay here, Owada. We're keeping this roof.

scenes.summary: The board gathers, and Mitsuhashi proposes a six-month trial in which half the roof stays a garden. Miyashita-sensei agrees to sign as advisor if the club pays for the melon bread.

ja: 時間どおりだ。全員、席につけ。
en: Right on time. Everyone, take a seat.

ja: 本日は屋上の件について結論を出す。
en: Today we reach a decision about the rooftop.

ja: 決める。ただし条件付きだ。
条件、数字で示してもらえますか。
en: Could you put the conditions in numbers?

ja: 六か月の試験運用とする。
屋上の半分は、菜園として残す。
en: Half the roof stays a garden.

ja: 残りは太陽光パネルの区画。
en: The other half goes to solar panels. Those are the terms.

ja: 技術的には、半分でも発電量は足りるかも。
en: Technically, half the roof might still produce enough power.
Numbers come later. Today we accept the terms.

ja: うわ、出た。校長の「あとで」。
まあまあ。半分なら、いいじゃないですか。
en: Come on. Half sounds fine to me.

ja: 宮下先生。顧問として署名できますか。
en: Miyashita-sensei. Will you sign as advisor?

ja: 部のお金で、メロンパン。人数分。
en: The club pays for the melon bread. One for everyone.

ja: 先生、それ条件じゃないです！
校長、それは正式な決議ですか。
en: Sir, is that an official resolution?

ja: 味は認める。だが、数字で出せ。
en: I'll admit the taste. Now show me numbers.

ja: 校長、トマト好きでしょ。
en: You like the tomatoes, don't you, sir?

scenes.summary: Minori and Haru worry the trial is a trap, but Minori says the deal is fair if they keep producing. Haru agrees, and they start planning the next harvest.

ja: 厳密に言うと、まだ半年しか守られてないよ。
en: Technically, we only have six months of protection.

ja: 半年たったら、どうなるの。
考えてもしょうがない。今は今。
en: Thinking about it won't help. Right now is what counts.

ja: でも、校長の提案、条件が多すぎない？
en: But the principal's offer has too many conditions, doesn't it?

ja: 収穫量が落ちたら、即打ち切りって書いてあった。
en: The fine print says if the yield drops, it's cancelled right away.
Are you saying it's a trap?

ja: 分からない。だから怖いの。
en: I don't know. That's why it scares me.

ja: 条件があるってことは、守れば続くってことでしょ。
en: If there are conditions, it keeps going as long as we meet them.

ja: 厳密には、公平な取引だと思う。収穫を続けるなら。
en: Technically, it's a fair deal, as long as we keep producing.

ja: 毎週、重さと糖度を測る。
記録はミノリがまとめて。
en: We weigh and measure the sugar every week.

ja: やる。トモエにも手伝わせる。
en: We will. I'll have Tomoe help too.

ja: トモエは数字を見ると、すぐ眠くなるよ。
en: Tomoe falls asleep the second she sees numbers.
Then she's in charge of naming things.
So, the next seedlings. What do we do?

ja: 接ぎ木の台木、まだ三本ある。
en: We still have three rootstocks for grafting.

ja: 一本は、赤い実の株に接ぐ。
en: One goes on the plant with the red fruit.

ja: 病気が出たら、どうするの。
葉を分けて育てる。隔離する。
en: We split the leaves and grow them apart.

ja: 水やりの時間、もう少し決めた方がいい。
en: We should set a fixed watering time too.

ja: 温度が下がってから水をやる。
en: Water once the heat has dropped.

ja: 了解。アブラムシ対策は？
テントウムシは、屋上に放すと逃げるよ。
en: Ladybugs fly off if you release them on a roof.

ja: じゃあ、逃げない理由を作る。
en: Then we give them a reason to stay.

ja: 次の収穫は、全部赤くする。
en: Next harvest, every single one turns red.

scenes.summary: Tomoe names the red tomato 'Kurenai' and the others argue about the name. Riku says it sounds like a sushi chef, and Tomoe refuses to change it.

en: Isn't that a bit too simple?

ja: 名前つけるなら、もっと考えようよ。
en: If we're going to name it, let's think harder.
Something a little more dignified, maybe?
Kurenai is what I came up with!

ja: 紅さん、寿司屋の大将っぽい。
en: Chef Kurenai. Sounds like a sushi shop owner, right?
It's not a shop owner! It's Kurenai!

ja: 技術的に、トマトは寿司ネタじゃない。
en: Technically, a tomato isn't a sushi topping.

ja: じゃあ、トマト寿司だな。
紅は紅！ トマトじゃない！
en: Kurenai is Kurenai! It's not a tomato!

ja: 変えないなら、ちゃんと呼べるように。
en: If we're keeping it, we should at least be able to say it. Kurenai, okay?

ja: 紅、いい響きだと思うけどね。
先生、メロンパン食べてるだけでしょ。
en: You're just eating melon bread, Sensei.

ja: 一番に赤くなった子だから！
en: Because it was the first one to turn red! I named it!

ja: 紅は、ここにいるこの子。
名前を聞けば、すぐ分かるでしょ？
en: Kurenai is this one, right here.
Once you hear the name, you'll know it.
Chef Kurenai of the sushi bar.

scenes.summary: Miyashita-sensei shows Riku the last trick of grafting as a farewell gift. He says Riku never really left the club, and Riku mutters a thank-you.

ja: ちょっと来なさい、大和田くん。
en: Come over here a second, Owada.
Oh, come on. Just humor me.

ja: 切り口で勝負が決まる。
en: Rootstock and scion. The cut decides everything.
I've heard that a hundred times.

ja: 角度は二十度。刃は寝かせて。
en: Twenty degrees, with the blade laid low.

ja: 目分量で切ると、必ず失敗する。
en: Eyeball it and you fail every time.
Ask Koizumi. She'd tell you the same.

ja: 小泉が聞いたら、数字持ってくるな。
en: If Koizumi heard that, she'd bring you numbers.

ja: だから、君が伝えなさい。
en: So you're the one who passes it on.

ja: 皮の内側の、薄い緑のところ。
en: The cambium. The thin green layer just under the bark.
Hold it up to the light and you'll see it.

ja: 合わせるのは、ここだけでいい。
en: You only need to line up this part.

ja: 全部合わせないと、くっつかないだろ。
en: Won't it stick if the whole cut doesn't match?

ja: 片側だけ合えば、くっつく。 植物は意外と許してくれる。
en: One side lining up is enough.
Plants are more forgiving than you'd think.

ja: そのくらいが、ちょうどいい。
en: A little sloppiness is just right.

ja: 先生が言うと、説得力ないな。
en: Coming from you, that's not very convincing.

ja: 合わせたら、テープで巻く。
en: Once it's matched, wrap it in tape.

ja: 巻き方くらい知ってる。
en: I know how to wrap it, at least.

ja: 知ってても、やらなかっただろ。
今日は君がやりなさい。
en: You knew how, but you never did it. You're doing it today.

ja: 君はずっと、この部に残ってた。
en: You never really left this club.

ja: 辞めたって言っただろ。
en: Don't make it sound like I came back.
Come up to the roof again sometime.

scenes.summary: At sunset, the club stands at the fence as the solar company's van drives away with its proposal shelved. They toast with melon bread, and Tomoe says the roof is theirs for now.

ja: 見て。バンが門を出ていく。
en: Look. The van's leaving through the gate.
They said the proposal's been shelved.

ja: 棚上げって、保留ってこと？
そういうこと。死んではいない。

en: ...Well, today can count as a win.
I've already got the bag open.

ja: 一人一個。数えたから間違いない。
en: One each. I counted, so it's accurate.

ja: 小泉さん、それは厳しすぎない？
en: Koizumi, isn't that a bit harsh?

ja: 厳しくないです。計算です。
先生は、もう半分食べたでしょ。
en: You already ate half of yours, Sensei.

ja: 半分は、会議の前の分だよ。
en: That half was from before the meeting.

ja: 屋上の夕日、きれいだね。
en: The sunset up here is beautiful.

ja: 毎日見てるのに、飽きないのが不思議。
en: I see it every day, and it never gets old.

ja: 夕日は、同じ場所から見ても同じじゃない。
en: The sunset never looks the same, even from the same spot.

ja: 先生、それ、いい話っぽいけど、ごまかしてる。
en: Sensei, that sounds nice, but you're dodging the question.

ja: メロンパンで乾杯って、どうなの。
en: A toast with melon bread? Really?

ja: 文化的には、まあ、ありです。
大和田くん、ちゃんと食べなさい。
食べてる。ちゃんと、食べてる。
今日は、いい色のトマトだった。
en: Today we got a good tomato.

ja: 赤くて、小さくて、ちゃんと赤かった。
屋上は、今はわたしたちのです！
en: The roof is ours, for now!

scenes.summary: Minori stands among a row of strawberry runners and teases that she has found a new crop to experiment with. She says someone is going to pick the wrong pot and cause a mess.

ja: 新しい作物、見つけちゃった。
en: Look what I found: a new crop to experiment with.

ja: それ、ただのランナーだろ。
実験は、いくらでもできる。
en: Runners can be multiplied, and there's no limit to experiments.

ja: 誰かが鉢を間違えて摘む。 絶対、混ざる。
en: Someone's going to pick the wrong pot.
And then it's going to be a total mess.
Next time, an experiment that starts before dawn.
Numbers don't lie, and they don't wait for anyone.
